question: The Commission recently decided to prioritise the development of the high-speed connection between Lisbon and Madrid, excluding the Vigo-Porto link from the core trans-European passenger transport network, which changes its estimated completion date to 2040. This clearly discriminates against Galicia and is a serious setback for the launch of this vital connection for Vigo and the surrounding area.

The high-speed rail connection between the cities of Vigo and Porto, known as the ‘southern exit’, has long been demanded by Galicia but has experienced constant delays. It is a strategic infrastructure project for the completion of the Atlantic Corridor rail link, and it is essential for the Vigo area as a lynchpin in the development of the Galicia-North Portugal Euroregion.
In view of the above, what steps will the Commission take to address this blatant discrimination in Galicia?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (7.6.2024) The trans-European transport network (TEN-T) as proposed by the Commission on 14 December 20211 has been defined on the basis of a common and transparent TEN-T methodology. The TEN-T core network includes priority sections of the network which can be expected to be completed by 2030.

The revised TEN-T regulation2, still to be adopted by the European Parliament and the Council, includes an additional network category, the extended core network, to be completed by 2040. The Porto-Vigo connection, which is part of the comprehensive network planned for completion in 2050 in the existing TEN-T Regulation3, has been upgraded to the extended core network in the revised TEN-T Regulation.

Nothing prevents the Member States to build the infrastructure on this connection at an earlier date. In terms of funding under the Connecting Europe Facility4 references to the ‘core network’ in Regulation (EU) 2021/11535 should be construed as including ‘extended core network’.
